title: Local to global almost everywhere: exhaustion of an open U by countably many balls W ⊂⊂ U
statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^N = Euclidean N be open, let μ be a measure on ℝ^N with μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0, and let P be a property of points of ℝ^N. Suppose that for every W ⊂⊂ U (IsRelCompactOpenIn W U) there is a set E ⊆ ℝ^N, not necessarily measurable, with μ(E) = 0 (outer measure) such that P(x) holds for every x ∈ W with x ∉ E. Then P(x) holds for μ-almost every x ∈ ℝ^N (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, P x).
lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (P : Euclidean N → Prop), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ W : Set (Euclidean N), IsRelCompactOpenIn W U → ∃ E : Set (Euclidean N), μ E = 0 ∧ ∀ x ∈ W, x ∉ E → P x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, P x
